utterances.text: Yes. Now, are you able to accurately describe the unconventional method? If you can, please do it. If you say, well, I have difficulties in doing it, then I'll not insist.

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is more straight-forward, at least in my mind. I believe what the individual in question did was he looked at the shrapnel pattern, and he stood at or near the centre of the crater, and he judged roughly where the centre line would be in the shrapnel pattern with a compass in his hand, and then he looked down at his compass and from that estimated the bearing for the direction of fire. So rather than identifying two points on the ground, it was simply a visual estimate of where the centre of the shrapnel pattern would be and shooting a bearing in that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now all depends here, if there is any difference, on how you choose the two points, the left and the right margin, to take as a starting point for your arch, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: It's difficult -- I'm not sure I understand what you mean, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it looks as if the arch used and the -- where the two arches meet, both above and under the centre of the crater, it all depends on where you start to draw your arch, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm beyond my technical -- the level of technical expertise that you're -- that you are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I'm --

utterances.speaker: MICHEL GAUTHIER
utterances.text: To be useful, to be honest. Because I'm -- I could not speak for Sergeant Dubant in this case in terms of how he located the centre of each arc. You can see the points on the graphic, but how he pin-pointed those on either side, top and bottom on the centre of the crater, and from those projected the arc on both sides, I don't know how he did that. And therefore I can't say how roughly that -- those points were estimated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. Any further questions, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No -- no -- I would just thank again our Canadian colleagues for assisting us this morning and everyone for getting up at an early hour to accommodate us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that on behalf of the Chamber we share this expression of gratitude for getting up early in the morning, and that's both for the witness, also for the representatives of the Canadian government, but finally of course for the representative of the Registry who shared this fate today. Mr. Gauthier, I usually thank people not only for answering all the questions that were put to them by the parties and by the Bench but also for coming a long way to The Hague. Now, fortunately there is no need to that. I don't know how long you travelled, but however long it has been, I wish you a safe return home. And we can conclude the videolink.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, of course, I also intended to thank the representatives of the Canadian government not only for getting up early but for assisting us.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLIMAN
utterances.text: [Via videolink] You're welcome, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then this concludes the videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we agreed that the there should be no further testimony heard today -- yes, the witness is excused. I see he is standing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would like to briefly deal with what was on my agenda, and I saw Mr. Tieger has left already, because I -- on the 17th of August of this year, some deadlines were set -- deadlines set for the 18th of September, and that was for the Defence to file any remaining evidentiary motions, including 92 bis and quater motions, that are not directly connected to the testimony of upcoming witnesses. We also invited the Prosecution to provisionally indicate whether it intends to present rebuttal evidence, and to the extent it does, what kind and how much. That information was given by Mr. Tieger earlier today. And he could do that because, since we are not sitting last Friday, the Chamber has informed the parties via an e-mail that any oral submissions in this respect could be made on the 21st of September. The Defence, however, apparently did not stick to this dead-line by filing today, which is not an oral submission, but by filing today the Defence motion pursuant to admit the evidence of Nedo Sevo pursuant to Rule 92 bis. I'm a bit puzzled by the title anyhow, by "pursuant to admit," but apart from that, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. We had some technical difficulties. There is also one other one that due to its size could not go through the e-mail system and thus we have do it on disk. And so there will be one other filing that is beyond the time-period that Your Honours had set that we would ask leave of the Court to file this one as well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for this one, what was the reason for this one to be filed late?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think it was just the timing, that it was already after the close of business that it was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you say it was late because it was late?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. And the other one was late because --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Due to the file size.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what was the file size that it's so extreme that it would --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: 10 megabytes. And apparently that is large enough -- it's approximately a hundred and -- I want to say, if I remember correctly, 126 or so pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that was 92 bis?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's a long statement, and then there's a translation, and that is how we come up with this rather large file size that the web mail server is unable to deal with. And then with that, I think we complete or should complete the 92 bis submissions except for there is the possibility of, I believe, one international Rule 70 witness that may not appear and then we might then file a Rule 92 bis for them. And that should be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. At least to the extent the Chamber of course allows you to file anything. I would -- we'll consider that, whether we will accept those, yes or no. I leave it to that for the time being. Now in terms of the remainder of the Defence case, the Chamber was informed through an informal communication that the Defence has approximately 30 witnesses left to be called including two proposed experts in relation to Tomasica whose reports have yet to be filed, and we would like to know whether that is accurate information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is accurate, Your Honours. The experts in question have only been recognised as experts within the last few weeks. When I say "recognised as experts," I should have said "appointed as experts by the Registry." I apologise for my inaccuracy in language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think we had some discussions about experts being appointed or not being appointed. And when were they now finally appointed by the Registry?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: My recollection is that the signed undertakings that commenced their appointment, at least one of them was sent by me last week, Monday. I don't know about the second one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We've seen the submissions by the Registrar on the 3rd of September, which is far a while ago, and do I understand that the instruction was given to the one expert you know of -- at what date was that? You said last week ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'm confused by what you mean by "instruction" and why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, to ask an expert to write a report. It's as simple as that. I mean, the whole issue of -- of being appointed and funded, et cetera, was -- well, at least we received quite some information from the Registry on that matter. I'd like to know when was the expert asked to write a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It would have been shortly after they were appointed by the Registry because that would be the first time that they are permitted to get the material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And do you have a date?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't as I stand here, Your Honours, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then we would like to hear from you later what date that was. Next question is: When do you think that you could present your last witness in court? Also without doubling times for examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I would have to check to be sure, but it was -- I believe our estimates went into sometime in November, early to mid-November I think was the estimates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please seek confirmation of that information so that we can put it on the record. And would that also deal with the -- would that include the expert witnesses who have not yet produced a report?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So your last witness is not really the last one but the last one apart from the --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Apart from the two --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- expert witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Apart from the two expert witnesses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two expert witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: The other expert witnesses would be completed by that month.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you give us any indication as when you expect those experts to present their reports so that they could be disclosed to the -- and could be presented to the Chamber under Rule - what is it? - 94 bis, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We have asked them to do so as soon as possible. I know one has sought some additional materials from the BH authorities, and as I stand here right now, I don't know the process -- I don't know the status of that request or any estimate as to when the reports would be completed. Obviously, we do recognise that under Rule 94 bis we would not be able to call them during the time-period that the 94 bis response period by the -- notification period by the Prosecution is adhered to. So we will obviously not schedule them to come testify before that time-period elapses from the filing of the 94 bis reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. But as soon as possible, of course, is a rather flexible moment to deliver something. You have no indication received yet and you have not suggested a dead-line for the experts?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm trying to be as precise as possible without misleading or approximating or guessing or fabricating an answer, since I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could we -- both in relation to the witnesses left to be called and the date of appointment or instruction of the expert witnesses and about any dead-lines given to those experts, could we receive detailed information not later than the day after tomorrow? That's by Wednesday, that we would know exactly this is the moment when the Registry accepted to appoint, this is when we instructed the expert, et cetera, because we will have a look at it also in -- against the background of the 3rd of September submissions made by the Registry.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we'll receive that information soon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What we could do now is to take a break of 20 minutes, and the only thing that would then be left are three relatively short items on my court agenda. We also could decide that we would continue for another seven or eight minutes and then adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're agreed to continue and finish in this session and then adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then I start with my first item which is a remaining issue from the testimony of Grujo Boric. During the testimony of this witness on the 23rd of April of this year, P7331 was reserved for excerpts from a transcript of a 2004 Prosecution interview with Boric. On the 4th of May, the Defence objected to its admission. On the 28th of August, the Office of the Prosecutor advised the Chamber and the Defence by e-mail that it had selected the excerpts, uploaded them under document bearing Rule 65 ter number 32422A and asked for the selection to be admitted. The Chamber hereby sets a dead-line of one week from today for the Defence to make any additional submissions on the record. My second and third item deal with remaining issues from the testimony of Radoje Vojvodic. The first one is about the replacement of P2560. During the testimony of this said witness on the 8th of September of this year, the Defence objected to the use of the word "hostage" in the English translation of P2560, which is an order by the VRS Main Staff signed by Mladic. This can be found at transcript page 38839. On the 9th of September, the Prosecution advised via an e-mail that it had uploaded a revised English translation into e-court under doc ID 0362-9386-A-ET. On the 17th of December, the Defence informed the Prosecution and the Chamber that it has no objection, and the Chamber therefore instructs the Registry to replace P2560 with the new version, at least as far as the English translation is concerned. And if I remember well, in the revised translation the word "hostage" does not further appear, but that's just from the top of my head. And then the last one is admission of D1225 and D1226. On the 8th of September of this year, D1225, a medical report, was marked for identification pending an English translation. The Chamber also understood that the Defence intended to tender document bearing 65 ter 1D06072, another medical report, also without an English translation. The Prosecution then informed the Chamber that the document bearing 65 ter number 33087 contained both medical reports with English translations. The Chamber marked for identification the document containing both reports as D1226, and this can be found at transcript pages 38798 to 38805. Can the Defence now confirm that both medical reports are in fact tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. We can confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then in order to avoid duplicating the evidentiary record, the Chamber hereby vacates D1225 and admits D1226 into evidence. And I have an empty court agenda again. We adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 22nd of September, 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, I.
